items.label: Abu Salim prison massacre
items.note: HRW says 'around/up to 1,200' (from a kitchen worker's meal count and exile groups; unverified); the Gaddafi Foundation (Aug 2009) counted at least 1,167 families of victims, and the NTC said in Sept 2011 the grave held 1,270 (from prison registers); no official list or confirmed body count exists, and Amnesty's 1996 releases said only 'scores'.

sources.t: HRW 2006: June 1996 killings at Abu Salim prison
Amnesty 2010: Abu Salim (up to 1,200; 1,167 families; no list)
Ahram Online, 25 Sep 2011: NTC says grave holds more than 1,270
Otago Daily Times: 1,270 estimated from prison registers
Reuters factbox (via El Economista): Foundation toll 1,167
Amnesty 1996 urgent action (mutiny, 'scores' killed)

items.label: Abu Salim: remains identified
items.note: I found no report of any victim being identified from the claimed 2011 grave (CNN saw only what looked like animal bones; the NTC lacked DNA capacity); a Libyan-justice group's statement likewise says bodies had not been found, and no verified list of names is public.

sources.t: CNN, 25 Sep 2011: reporters saw apparent animal bones
Amnesty, Sept 2011: protect the site, link to Abu Salim not confirmed
HRW, 26 Sep 2011: cannot confirm grave location
Libyan Justice statement (1,260 killed; bodies still to be found)

items.label: Abu Salim: families notified
items.note: Libyan Human Rights Solidarity (Switzerland) told HRW that authorities had notified 112 families since 2001 that a relative was dead, and that 238 families had lost contact with a relative held there; these are counts of families, not of deaths.

sources.t: HRW 2006: June 1996 killings at Abu Salim prison

items.label: Public hangings and televised executions
items.note: Only isolated cases are documented: students Omar Dabboub and Mohamed Ben Saoud hanged in Benghazi on 7 April 1977 (a historian adds two more names), and six civilians hanged and three soldiers shot on television in February 1987 (US State Dept); no total for the period exists.

sources.t: Project notes: 7 April events (Dabboub, Asharq Al-Awsat, IRB Canada)
Asharq Al-Awsat on 1977 hangings
US State Dept Country Report on Human Rights 1987 (via ecoi.net)

items.label: February 1987 televised executions
items.note: US State Department report: six civilians hanged in public and three military personnel shot, televised; it adds the number of political killings in 1987 is unknown.

sources.t: US State Dept Country Report on Human Rights 1987 (via ecoi.net)

items.label: Executions after 1984 Bab al-Aziziya attack
items.note: Reuters factbox says an unknown number were executed and thousands jailed (unattributed); Amnesty (1992) says most people arrested after the May 1984 attack were believed held at Abu Salim, with no execution total, so I give no number.

sources.t: Reuters factbox on Gaddafi rule (via El Economista)
Amnesty 1992: further information on political detention

items.label: Exiles killed abroad ('stray dogs')
items.note: Amnesty recorded at least 37 attacks on Libyan opponents abroad with 25 deaths, March 1980 to June 1987 (quoted by the US State Dept); a Wikipedia summary of one scholar says at least 35 opposition figures; UPI's 1981 list names ten killed in 1980-81 in Italy (5), UK (2), West Germany, Greece and the USA.

sources.t: US State Dept Country Report 1987, quoting Amnesty: 37 attacks, 25 deaths
UPI, 12 Nov 1981: Libyan hit squad victims
Wikipedia: Reception and legacy of Muammar Gaddafi (at least 35)

items.label: Firing-squad executions, 30 May 2010
items.note: Amnesty reported 18 people shot by firing squad (14 in Tripoli, 4 in Benghazi); these were judicial executions, not all political, and I did not find a full count of judicial executions across the period.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Human rights in Libya under Muammar Gaddafi (citing Amnesty press release)

items.label: Known political prisoners
items.note: Amnesty named 77 prisoners of conscience and 144 political prisoners in 1987 and at least 554 by 1992, and said true numbers were much higher; there is no reliable total across 1969-2011.

sources.t: US State Dept Country Report 1987, quoting Amnesty
Amnesty 1992: at least 554 political prisoners

items.label: Enforced disappearances, 1970s to 1990s
items.note: Amnesty says 'hundreds of cases' from the 1970s to 1990s remained unresolved in 2010; no verified total for the Gaddafi era exists.

sources.t: Amnesty annual report 2010: Libya

items.label: People missing in Libya, all periods
items.note: The Libyan government said in 2012 up to 10,000 were unaccounted for (cited by ICMP, which also quotes a figure of about 10,000 in 2020), the ICRC had registered about 1,600 in 2020, and a 2025-era Authority figure of 7,169 is reported by Asharq Al-Awsat; none of these are split by Gaddafi era, 2011 or later, and ICMP's page lists Chad, Uganda and Egypt wars, Abu Salim, 2011 and later events together.

sources.t: ICMP: Libya programme
ICMP: Where are the missing, Libya
Al Jazeera, Aug 2020: about 10,000 (ICMP); ICRC about 1,600
Asharq Al-Awsat: 7,169 missing (Authority)

items.label: Missing after the 2011 uprising
items.note: Government officials said in 2013 a little more than 2,000 were still missing and 2,135 cases were filed in a year (mostly rebels and loyalists missing from 2011); in Dec 2011 an unattributed 10,000 was widely quoted; Jan 2013 government said about 2,100 missing, so these mix victims of both sides.

sources.t: The World, Aug 2013: ministry figures
Al Jazeera, Dec 2011: estimated 10,000 missing
Wikipedia: Casualties of the Libyan civil war (2011) (Jan 2013 government figures)

items.label: Bin Jawad grave (rebels killed 2011)
items.note: A Libyan missing-persons committee recovered 163 bodies near Bin Jawad east of Sirte in 2012, of about 400 missing from eastern Libya, killed Feb-Mar 2011 partly in combat and partly by execution (AFP).

sources.t: IOL / Sapa-AFP, 5 Mar 2012: mass grave found in Libya

items.label: Tripoli crackdown, 20-22 February 2011
items.note: HRW relayed doctors' reports of at least 62 dead in two hospitals (unverified by HRW); doctors told the UN Commission of Inquiry more than 200 bodies reached morgues on 20-21 Feb; the ICC prosecutor estimated 500-700 killed nationwide by security forces in February.

sources.t: HRW, 22 Feb 2011
UN Commission of Inquiry report A/HRC/19/68
Wikipedia: Libyan civil war 2011 (ICC 500-700)

items.label: Yarmouk/Khamis Brigade warehouse
items.note: On 23 Aug 2011 HRW counted about 45 remains in the burned warehouse (153 names read at roll call; survivors estimated about 20), while the UN Commission lists 157 detainees with only 51 survivors confirmed and says 'dozens' were killed; no agreed death count.

sources.t: HRW, 29 Aug 2011
UN Commission of Inquiry report A/HRC/19/68

items.label: Gargur and Bab al-Aziziya killings
items.note: The UN Commission reports 21 shot at Gargur on 23 Aug and 15 bodies at Bab al-Aziziya; HRW found 17 detainees killed at the Internal Security building, 18 bodies in a riverbed and 29 near a field clinic (overlaps possible).

sources.t: HRW, 28 Aug 2011
UN Commission of Inquiry report A/HRC/19/68

items.label: Civilians deliberately killed by regime forces, 2011
items.note: No national count of people killed by regime forces exists; UCDP codes 152-168 civilians deliberately killed by pro-Gaddafi forces (as summarised by Wikipedia), while the ICC prosecutor estimated 500-700 killed in February alone; the two measure different things.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Casualties of the Libyan civil war (2011)
Wikipedia: Libyan civil war 2011 (ICC 500-700)

items.label: Total 2011 war deaths, context only (both sides)
items.note: NTC claimed 30,000 (Sept 2011) and its justice minister told the UN 20,000; the Libyan government said in 2013 about 4,700 rebels and a similar number of loyalists; ACLED counts 6,109 and UCDP 1,914-3,466; these include fighters and are not victims of the regime alone.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Casualties of the Libyan civil war (2011)
Ahram Online: NTC says more than 30,000 killed
El Espectador/EFE, 19 Sep 2011: 20,000 told to UN

items.label: Pan Am 103, Lockerbie
items.note: 259 on board plus 11 on the ground; Megrahi was convicted in 2001 and Libya accepted responsibility for its officials' actions in 2003, though Gaddafi denied ordering it.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Pan Am Flight 103

items.label: UTA Flight 772
items.note: All 170 aboard died; six Libyans including Abdullah Senussi were convicted in absentia in France in 1999, and Libya paid compensation in 2004.

sources.t: Wikipedia: UTA Flight 772

items.label: La Belle discotheque bombing, Berlin
items.note: Three died and about 230 were hurt; a German court in 2001 found it was planned by Libyan intelligence and embassy, but did not prove Gaddafi's involvement.

sources.t: Wikipedia: 1986 Berlin discotheque bombing

items.label: WPC Yvonne Fletcher, London
items.note: Shot from the Libyan People's Bureau on 17 April 1984, with 11 demonstrators wounded; Libya accepted general responsibility in 1999.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Yvonne Fletcher

items.label: Total victims of the regime
items.note: I found no official Libyan or UN total; every figure above comes from a different counter with different methods, so they must not be summed.

sources.t: UN Commission of Inquiry report A/HRC/19/68 (no total given)
ICMP: Libya programme (government estimate of up to 10,000 unaccounted for)

summary: The best-documented single atrocity is the Abu Salim prison massacre of June 1996, with about 1,200 prisoners reported killed (range 1,167 to 1,270, counted by Human Rights Watch, the Gaddafi Foundation and the 2011 transitional council); no verified list of names or identified remains is public. Smaller events are better documented: at least 25 exiles killed abroad in 1980-1987 (Amnesty), the 2011 Tripoli killings (62 to over 200 in February, about 45 to 157 in the Yarmouk warehouse) and the foreign bombings (Lockerbie 270, UTA 772 170, La Belle 3, Fletcher 1). There is no official or UN total for victims of the regime, and counts of political prisoners, executions and the disappeared are partial. Missing-persons figures (up to 10,000) mix the Gaddafi era, 2011 and later and have never been broken down by period; 2011 war totals (about 2,000 to 30,000) include fighters on both sides.
